title: ECP Trust Registration Record (M3-RG0 — immutable after acceptance)
description: The immutable registration record established by the Registration Authority when a package is accepted into the protected registration boundary (M3-RG0, 0.7.0, order §5). It preserves: case identity; the full commitment set (case content, ground truth, success criterion, environment, provenance, originating package); the six Owner-bound ruling citations frozen at acceptance; the authority decision; the gate snapshot under which acceptance occurred; the deterministic registration identity (authority-assigned, monotone); and the lineage index of the accepting event (the event carries the record hash — bidirectional binding without circular hashing). The file is write-once; any correction is a NEW registration-amendment event, never an edit. registration_hash = SHA-256 over the ECP-CANONICAL-JSON-1.0 serialization with registration_hash removed; record_hash (computed by the verifier/lineage) additionally covers the populated registration_hash field. Real records live only in a private trust area; public illustrations under examples/ must be format-illustration records with real recomputable hashes.

content_class.description: 'review' = real registration material (private trust area only); 'format-illustration' = public dummy (examples/ only).

registration_id.description: Deterministic identity assigned by the Registration Authority (monotone; never author-chosen).

owner_ruling_citations.description: The six rulings frozen at acceptance — an accepted record can never carry a null citation (acceptance required them).

gate.description: Snapshot of the gate state under which acceptance occurred — acceptance is only legal while the gate is OPEN.

event_index.description: Index of the registration-accepted lineage event; the event carries this record's record_hash (bidirectional binding).

immutability.const: append-only — the original record is never rewritten; corrections are new registration-amendment events; the original commitments remain independently verifiable
